scope: Test whether the existing MAME host capture route can be repeated and whether small/slow xdotool relative steps give a stable path to an enabled VUE arrow.

evidence.observation: After mapping/focusing the authenticated MAME window and the previously successful blank-area click gesture, the pointer appeared at the lower-left screen edge; the capture hook remained captured=false.
Calling the existing hook's capture() safely enabled mouse input and cleared wait_button_up, but the pointer remained at the lower-left edge.
A small relative +10,+10 host movement produced no visible guest cursor displacement.
A subsequent +100,0 movement moved the edge cursor only about 7 guest pixels.

result: The hook's capture() method itself reliably re-enabled the configured MAME mouse without a second hook. The xdotool route is still not a predictable coordinate mapping: the repeated click did not capture; the pointer appeared at an edge; +10,+10 was below visible displacement and +100,0 produced only about +7 px. No scrollbar or application control was clicked, so there is no held-state or scrolling evidence.
next: Continue only I167. Find a repeatable way to map relative input to the cursor using the existing capture hook without relying on large instantaneous XTest warps. Keep the same enabled VUE scrollbar target; press only after a fresh native image visibly places the cursor hotspot inside it. Otherwise retain this as an unresolved input-path limit and do not claim the GTK2 pressed state.
